name: Hills and Winding Path — Loose Ink and Wash
subject: hills

styleSelection.reason: Loose ink-and-wash landscape combining a full five-band light-to-dark watercolor value architecture (pale buff path with reserved glints, sunlit yellow-green hills, nested middle foliage layers, regional Band 3 modeling, cool ultramarine-sepia shadow glazes, and deep tree recesses) with preparatory structural ink and comprehensive closing dip-pen ink linework on dry paper.

families.notes: Warm sandy buff and pale sienna dirt road curving from the lower right around the left-center bend to the upper forks; brightest glints reserved as bare cream paper while the roadbed holds a dilute warm Band 1 glaze protected by litLift from middle and shadow foliage washes.

Dense rounded oak canopies crowning the upper ridge on both sides of the upper forks, built from sap-green and olive middle washes into ultramarine-sepia shadow glazes and scalloped closing ink contours.
Sunlit yellow-green grassy slope on the upper-left and middle-left flank of the winding road, graded from bright hansa-yellow and sap-green light washes into warm olive midtones.

Central grassy hillside and rounded oak/chaparral foliage masses nestled inside the main S-curve of the path, transitioning from bright sunlit grass to deep cool-green and slate-sepia foliage shadows.
Right-hand hillside pasture and overarching dark tree masses with regional Band 3 foliage modeling and bold contour ink along the road cut.
Lower foreground road shoulders, warm sandy ruts, and dark framing chaparral/oak masses in the lower-left and lower-right corners.
